newsitem.title: USA: Phelps invests abroad, hikes reserves at home.
newsitem.headline: Phelps invests abroad, hikes reserves at home.

text.p: Phelps Dodge Corp will spend about $500 million on capital this year as the company moves ahead with projects in new countries, and expands existing operations and reserves, Douglas Yearley, Phelp's president, chairman and CEO said.
Depreciation was running at $250 million a year, and probably rising to $300 million by early next year.

This summer Phelps will inaugurate its first project in China, Yearley told Reuters. The company stumped up less than half the $25 million spent on building a new high voltage cable plant in a northern province.

And Phelps recently took a small stake in the Kazakh copper mine and smelter, Balkhashmys, the U.S. company's first involvement in the Former Soviet Union. Nevertheless Phelps is initially limiting itself to offering technical assistance and no large cash injection, Yearley said.

Although the expansion of Phelps' Candelaria mine in Chile will make the company slightly long in concentrates, Yearley said there were no plans yet to hike smelter output on its own or with another company such as Enami.
At present 55 percent of Phelps' mined copper output was in concentrates which needed smelting, the balance was from oxide deposits leached into electrowon cathode.

Phelps has enough copper reserves for at least 20 years at present production levels. "We are adding to it faster than we are using it right now," Yearley said. Some $50 million a year was spent on exploration.

"Morenci has long term potential for both sulphide and SX/ EW, and we have just expanded reserves at our Tyrone mine to 2005," Yearley said. Reserves at Tyrone now total about 1 billion pounds of copper.

"Chino has added reserves, and there is potential for more there, and the Safford project has yet to be developed has a very large reserve, maybe 12 billion pounds of copper in the ground," Yearley said.
Morenci and Safford are located in Arizona, with Chino and Tyrone in New Mexico.
Phelps' copper production target of 2.2 billion pounds by 2002 did not depend on a new discovery, Yearley said.
